questions.stem: In the assignment’s face-analysis pipeline, a detector first finds a face and a crop of that region is passed to an expression estimator. What does the cropping operation itself accomplish?
assumptions: Educational pipeline only; no actual image, identity inference or runtime claim.

options.text: It assigns the final expression label before the estimator runs.
It selects the facial region of interest for subsequent analysis.
It retains every background pixel while only changing the expression-label vocabulary.
It establishes the person’s true internal emotional state from the selected pixels.

questions.stem: A facial-analysis task takes 80 ms and an independent speech task takes 120 ms. Both start at t=0, run without resource contention, and have zero fusion overhead. At what time are both results first available, and how much earlier is that than running the tasks serially?
assumptions: Simultaneous starts; durations fixed; no queueing, contention, startup or fusion delay; toy supplied timings, not hardware benchmarks.

options.text: 200 ms; no time saved.
40 ms; 160 ms earlier.
80 ms; 120 ms earlier.
120 ms; 80 ms earlier.

options.text: Stereo vision with no active infrared projection in the described setup.

Time-of-flight ranging instead of stereo correspondence.
Stereo vision together with active infrared projection.

questions.stem: In a supplied ideal motion exercise, a robot moves by perpendicular displacements 300 mm horizontally and 200 mm vertically along one straight segment, returns along that segment, and repeats this round trip 12 times. Assume constant speed equal to 60% of the supplied 8.2 m/s, with instantaneous reversals and no acceleration time. What are total path length and elapsed motion time, rounded only at the end to two decimals?
questions.subtopic: Straight-line round trips and ideal travel time

questions.stem: Two systems both estimate a robot’s pose. System A localizes against an existing occupancy map using LiDAR and odometry; System B jointly estimates the map and robot pose. In the assignment’s comparison, which role assignment is correct?
questions.subtopic: AMCL versus joint mapping and localization
assumptions: Use the assignment’s existing-map localization versus SLAM workflow comparison; do not infer that either module is itself the route planner.

options.text: A is map construction without pose estimation; B is localization without map estimation.
A is global route planning; B is local velocity-command generation.
A corresponds to AMCL localization; B corresponds to SLAM.
A corresponds to SLAM; B corresponds to AMCL localization.

questions.stem: Which statement preserves the assignment’s stated reasons for using ROS 2 in autonomous navigation without turning its phrase “real-time navigation” into an unconditional hard-deadline guarantee?
questions.subtopic: ROS 2 navigation motivation and timing scope
assumptions: Source interpretation only; no ROS runtime, QoS-document lookup, measured deadline or hard-real-time certification claimed.

options.text: Its modular architecture makes every navigation callback meet every deadline regardless of execution load.
It combines modular architecture, sensor integration and support for timely navigation; a specific deadline still needs system-level validation.
A visualization display alone certifies that the navigation pipeline meets its control deadlines.
Sensor integration removes the need to account for scheduling and communication delays.

questions.stem: In the assignment’s specific setup, a 360° planar LiDAR scans at a fixed height and an RGB-D camera sees a low obstacle that does not intersect that scan plane. The camera observes valid depth for the obstacle and the sensors are calibrated into a common frame. Why can fusing them improve the local costmap?
assumptions: The particular stated planar sensor configuration; obstacle within camera field of view with valid depth; known common-frame calibration; no claim that fusion detects every obstacle.

options.text: The camera can add obstacle evidence missed by the scan plane while the LiDAR retains its wider angular coverage.
The low obstacle must be absent from the scene because no LiDAR return intersected it.
The camera’s local field of view replaces every direction in the LiDAR’s 360° scan.
Using two sensors makes frame alignment and measurement validity irrelevant to the costmap.

citations.locator: Assignment physical page 58: Week 12 item 7, sensor-combination prompt, choices and explanatory contrast

questions.stem: For an ideal no-slip differential drive, let wheel radius r=0.1 m, axle separation L=0.5 m, right wheel rate ωᵣ=+5 rad/s and left wheel rate ωₗ=−5 rad/s. Positive wheel rates mean forward rolling, v=r(ωᵣ+ωₗ)/2 at the axle midpoint, and yaw rate Ω=r(ωᵣ−ωₗ)/L. Which motion results?
questions.subtopic: Differential drive with opposite wheel rates
assumptions: Ideal rolling without slip; equal radii; flat plane; L is full wheel separation; stated positive-forward wheel and right-minus-left yaw conventions.

options.text: v=0 m/s and Ω=+2 rad/s: in-place rotation.
v=+0.5 m/s and Ω=0 rad/s: straight translation.
v=0 m/s and Ω=0 rad/s: no body motion.
v=0 m/s and Ω=−2 rad/s: opposite-sign in-place rotation.

questions.stem: A robot nearly hits a worker, but no injury occurs. Under the safety-learning principle stated in the assignment, what should the engineering team do with this event?

options.text: Wait for a repeated collision before considering the event relevant to safety review.
Record the near-miss and review its causes, even though no injury occurred.
Record it only if an injury or property-damage claim is later filed.
Review it informally but omit a record because there is no measured harm.

questions.stem: Which feature in the assignment is a physical yielding mechanism that can take up impact energy without first relying on software to command a stop?

assumptions: Compare the physical mechanism, not overall system safety certification; compliance can store and later return energy, so absorption is not assumed to mean irreversible dissipation.

options.text: Mechanical compliance in soft joints or back-drivable actuation.
Emergency-stop decision logic while retaining an otherwise rigid contact path.
Software-defined safety zones while retaining an otherwise rigid contact path.
Redundant sensing while retaining an otherwise rigid contact path.
